title: Longest unique substring window
assumptions: Assume ordinary Python string indexing and average O(1) dictionary operations.
rationale: Single pass; left only moves forward and each dictionary operation is O(1) on average, so the work is linear in len(text).

title: Insertion sort
assumptions: Worst case is a reverse-sorted integer array; assume primitive array access and arithmetic are O(1).
rationale: On a reverse-sorted array each element shifts past all earlier ones, giving 1 + 2 + ... + (n-1) = n(n-1)/2 shifts.

title: Longest increasing subsequence by dynamic programming
assumptions: Input is an integer list; analyze the implementation shown, not alternative algorithms.
rationale: The nested loops run i from 0 to n-1 with j < i, about n(n-1)/2 constant-time comparisons and updates.

title: Reachable vertices with breadth-first search
assumptions: The input is an adjacency-list graph with V vertices and E listed edges; analyze in V and E.
rationale: Each reachable vertex is enqueued once thanks to seen, and each adjacency list is scanned once, so every listed edge is examined at most once.

title: Binary tree height
assumptions: The input is a finite binary tree without cycles or shared child nodes; each node is processed once if reached.
rationale: Each node is visited exactly once with O(1) work per call, for n nodes. Recursion depth is O(h), which is O(n) in the worst case of a skewed tree.
